title: README with screenshots
description: A README worth landing on: what Beady is, a screenshot of the list and one of the board or tree (rendered by the offscreen snapshot mode, light and dark), the safety story for writes, install instructions, and the keyboard map.

title: Appearance and text size settings
description: A Settings window (CMD-,): Appearance System/Light/Dark, a theme picker for each of dark and light, and a text size (Small, Default, Large, Extra Large) that scales the whole UI. Honour the system's Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency settings. Persist in UserDefaults.
close_reason: Settings window (CMD-,) with appearance, a theme per mode and text size; CMD-T theme sheet with live swatches; every theme, appearance and text size is also a palette command. macOS Increase Contrast overrides with the high-contrast theme, watched live. All persisted in UserDefaults.

title: Apply tokens across the UI
description: Replace every hard-coded colour (Badges.swift category/priority colours, the orange activity banner, green progress, drop highlights) with tokens from the environment, so a theme change repaints everything.
close_reason: Every meaningful colour now comes from the theme in the environment: status categories, priorities, blocked, progress, drop targets, selection borders, warning banners and the focus breadcrumb. No literal colours left in the views.

title: Appearance: themes, contrast and text size
description: The app currently inherits macOS light/dark through SwiftUI's semantic colours, but every accent (status, priority, blocked, progress) is hard-coded, there is no appearance control, no text-size control, and nothing verifies contrast. Move all colour to design tokens, ship System plus the three best-known dark and light themes, add a high-contrast pair for poor eyesight, and prove the contrast ratios in tests. Blocks the public repo push.

title: Design tokens and themes, with contrast proved by tests
description: A Theme of semantic tokens (surfaces, text, border, accent, the four status categories, priorities, blocked, pinned, starred, selection) as plain RGB in BeadsPresentation so it stays testable and SwiftUI-free. Themes: System (macOS semantic), and the best-known three dark (Dracula, One Dark, Nord) and three light (Solarized Light, GitHub Light, One Light), plus a High Contrast pair. Tests compute WCAG contrast ratios: every theme's body text on its background clears 4.5:1, status and priority colours clear 3:1 against their surface, and the high-contrast pair clears 7:1.
close_reason: Theme/ThemeColors/RGB in BeadsPresentation with WCAG contrast maths; 8 themes (Dracula, One Dark, Nord, Solarized Light, GitHub Light, One Light + a high-contrast pair). Tests prove body text >= 4.5:1, status/priority/accents >= 3:1, and >= 7:1 for the high-contrast pair.

title: Data: add and remove labels through the gateway
description: BDCommand cases for 'bd update --add-label=/--remove-label= --json -- <id>', an IssueChange.setMark case, validation (no-op when already in that state) and read-back verification that the label is or isn't there.

title: Presentation: pin and star actions, Starred view, starred filter
description: model.toggleMark for a bead; pinned-first everywhere; a Starred entry in the sidebar with its count; a one-click starred filter that reuses the existing labels filter so it reads as a normal chip; palette commands for all of it.

title: Core: marks, pinned-first ordering, label views
description: IssueMark (pinned/starred) naming the bd labels in one place; Issue.has(mark); sorting that floats pinned to the top of any ordering, inside groups and board columns and among tree siblings; ViewSource.label(String) so a view can be any label, which is what the Starred view is.

title: Pinned and starred, carried by bd labels
description: Pin (label 'pinned') floats zero or more beads to the top of every list, tree and board column, within whatever filters are active. Star (label 'starred') gets a dedicated view and a one-click filter. State lives in bd labels, never in app preferences, so any bd client sees the same thing. Note: bd also has a built-in 'pinned' STATUS in the frozen category; the label is separate from it, and the label names live in one constant (IssueMark) if we ever want to rename them.

title: Palette should match natural command names
description: Owner: typing 'fin' in CMD-P should filter to a Find command and ENTER should run it (focus the search box). Today commands only match their exact titles, so 'fin' finds nothing ('Search This View'). Give every command aliases/keywords and match against them, and rename the search command to Find.
close_reason: Every command now carries keywords, matched with a lower weight than its title, and the search command is titled 'Find in This View'. Tested: fin/find -> Find, reload -> Refresh, kanban -> Board, column -> Display, help -> Shortcuts; Return runs the highlighted row as before.

title: Rename the product to Beady
description: Owner picked Beady (plays on bitsby.me; a beady eye is a watchful one, and the chosen icon reads as one). Touches: executable and target name, bundle id me.bitsby.beady, window title, app path build/Beady.app, BEADS_VIEWER_* env vars, the .beads-viewer-scratch write-test marker, dispatch queue labels, README, release workflow, and the local directory ~/projects/beady.
close_reason: Beady it is. Renamed across the executable, bundle id (me.bitsby.beady), window title, env vars, scratch marker, scripts, README and the local checkout (~/projects/beady). GitHub repo not created yet: publishing is the owner's call.

title: Name the product and create the GitHub repo
description: Repo goes under github.com/dvhthomas. Name undecided; bv is taken by beads' own viewer. Creating and pushing the repo publishes the code, so it waits for the owner's go-ahead.

title: Initial git commit
description: ~8,900 lines of source and tests exist only in the working tree: no history, no rollback, nothing to bisect.
close_reason: Three commits: bd's own init, the app (70 files), and the tracker state. CFBundleVersion now reads 3 from the commit count.

title: Distribution 1: build from source
description: README section: clone, scripts/bundle.sh, open build/BeadsViewer.app. A locally built app is never quarantined, so this path has no Gatekeeper friction. State the requirements (macOS 15+, Swift 6 toolchain, bd on PATH).
close_reason: README Install section leads with clone + scripts/bundle.sh, noting that a locally built app is never quarantined, plus requirements and a Developing section.

title: App icon: lifecycle ring (concept C)
description: Owner picked concept C. Tune the ring for 32px legibility, render the full iconset, build BeadsViewer.icns with iconutil, ship it in Resources/, and set CFBundleIconFile in scripts/bundle.sh.
close_reason: Concept C rendered by scripts/make-icon.swift (reproducible), tuned for small sizes, shipped as Resources/AppIcon.icns and wired into bundle.sh; verified at 128 and 32 px.

title: Ready for distribution
description: Everything between the working app and a repo other people can clone or download: icon, packaging, licence, release process, and the review items still open.

title: Unblock path and neighbourhood graph for a selected bead
description:
Question to answer: for this blocked bead, what chain of work has to finish first? bd already computes it (bd graph lays out execution order, layer 0 = startable now; bd dep/blocked expose the edges).

Proposed UX, to keep the main UI calm:
1. Details inspector gains an 'Unblock path' section - an ordered, clickable list grouped by layer ('Start now', 'Then', ...), shown only when the bead is actually blocked. Text answers the question without a canvas.
2. A Graph sheet (CMD-G) for the picture: the selected bead's neighbourhood only - blockers upstream, dependents downstream, children below - laid out left to right by layer, drawn in SwiftUI Canvas. A sheet, not a fourth layout, so the list/tree/board UI is untouched.
3. Layers computed in BeadsCore from the snapshot (deps are already loaded) so it is instant and unit-testable, with an opt-in integration test comparing against real 'bd graph' output, the way Ready parity was checked against 'bd ready'.

title: Remember each view's filters between launches
description: Today only the last lifecycle view, the column layout and the recent workspaces persist (UserDefaults, ~/Library/Preferences/me.bitsby.beady.plist). Per-view filters, grouping, ordering and layout are in-memory only, so they're lost on quit. Persist the ViewState map.

title: UI: pin and star affordances
description: Row context menu, details panel buttons, and a marker in the row so a pinned or starred bead is visible at a glance. Marks are additive, reversible metadata, so they apply immediately through ChangeRunner (validate, write, verify) rather than going through the confirmation sheet - unlike edits, which keep it.

title: Layout switcher in the view header
description: Owner: a quick List / Tree / Board toggle directly in the main UI (segmented control in the filter bar), keeping the same option in the Display popover.
close_reason: Segmented List/Tree/Board control in the view header, next to Display, which keeps the same picker. Both read their names and symbols from DisplayText.layout(Symbol).

title: Hover preview for truncated cell text
description: Owner: hovering a column whose text is cut off should show the full text, wrapped, capped at 512 characters with an ellipsis when there is more. Applies to title, id, labels and assignee cells, and to tree and board rows.
close_reason: DisplayText.preview cuts at 512 characters on a word boundary with an ellipsis, and is used as the hover tooltip on id, title, labels and assignee cells plus tree rows and board cards. Tested as a pure function.

title: Help menu should teach the ? shortcut
description: Owner: the Help menu needs an item making it discoverable that ? opens the shortcut sheet. A menu item can only display one key (the menu binds CMD-/), so add a hint row alongside it.
close_reason: Help menu now has Keyboard Shortcuts (CMD-/), a hint row 'Press ? anywhere in the window for the shortcut list' since a menu item can only display one key, and a link to the repo.

title: Distribution 2: GitHub Release zip
description: scripts/release.sh building a release-config bundle and zipping it with ditto, plus a tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow that attaches the zip. Release notes must tell people how to get past Gatekeeper on an unsigned app: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, or xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine.
close_reason: scripts/release.sh builds a release-config bundle and zips it with ditto (verified: 1.1MB zip unpacks to an ad-hoc signed app); .github/workflows/release.yml tests, builds and attaches it on a v* tag, with Gatekeeper instructions in the release notes.

title: LICENSE
description: No licence file. Without one the code is all-rights-reserved, which makes a public repo useless to anyone else.
close_reason: MIT, matching the norm for a small tool; copyright Dylan Thomas. Easy to change before the repo is public.

title: Owner check: single-key shortcuts while typing
description: Verify by hand that typing f, /, ? and V into the search field and the edit forms inserts the character instead of triggering Filter / Search / Shortcuts / Display. The shortcuts now stand down while search has focus (FilterBarView.singleKey); the edit-form case is unverified.

title: Palette and help show the keys that are actually bound
description: AppCommand.shortcut is display text maintained separately from the menu bar's KeyboardShortcut bindings (BeadsViewerApp.swift). They agree today but can drift: e.g. focusSearch shows / while the Edit menu binds CMD-F. Make one source of truth, or show both keys.
close_reason: AppCommand.bindings is now the only place keys are declared; the menu bar takes its ⌘ shortcut and the in-window buttons take the plain key from the same list, and the palette/help text is derived from it.

title: Build number from git, not a hard-coded 1
description: CFBundleVersion is pinned to 1 in scripts/bundle.sh, so every build looks identical to macOS. Derive it from the git commit count.
close_reason: CFBundleVersion is now the git commit count and CFBundleShortVersionString comes from the VERSION file, so both scripts read one source.

title: Stop parsing interaction-log lines older than the window
description: BDGateway.recentActivity re-reads and parses up to 256KB of .beads/interactions.jsonl on every reload. Scan from the end and stop at the first entry older than 'since'.
close_reason: Not done as specified: the 256KB tail cap already bounds the work, and stopping at the first old record would silently hide another session's writes if the log were ever out of order - the one thing this feature exists to report. Kept the bounded full scan, now reading newest-first, with the reasoning in the code.
